issues.issue: The preamble makes the Borrower a party ('made by and between EGL ... and ESSAR STEEL MINNESOTA LLC'), yet the cover page describes the instrument as 'made by ESSAR GLOBAL LIMITED in favor of ICICI' and Section 4.08 Integration recites only 'the agreement of the Guarantor, the Facility Agent and the Lenders'. Whether the Borrower is an obligated party to this guarantee is left genuinely open.

The recital that 'EGL will derive substantial direct and indirect benefit' states a conclusion about consideration that no operative provision supports, and it sits against the Article III(e) solvency representation in a fraudulent-transfer context. A court could be asked whether the recital binds on the benefit question.

The recital says the Agreement is delivered 'for the ratable benefit of the Lenders', while Section 2.01(a)(ii) requires funding to be provided to the Borrower and Section 4.15 denies rights to any non-party Person. The recital and those operative terms point in different directions about who benefits.

Core operative terms such as 'Commercial Operations Date', 'Project', 'Permitted Project Change' and 'Required Lenders' are left to the Credit Agreement, while Section 1.03 says this Agreement governs over any other Loan Document. Which document supplies meaning could be contested.

The definition piles 'the Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement)' onto 'all other obligations and liabilities of the Borrower' with a disjunctive 'or the LC Exposure', so the outer boundary of the guaranteed debt is not fixed by the words. The reach of 'all other obligations and liabilities' is exactly what a guarantor would litigate.

'Deficiency' means 'any actual shortfall, howsoever caused, in funds available to the Borrower required: ... (ii) any increase in the cost of the Project', which does not parse with the lead-in and leaves clause (ii) overlapping clause (i); the opening words 'as determined by the Borrower or the Required Lenders' also leave it unclear who has the determining voice and whether that determination is conclusive. Both the trigger and the measuring party are open to two readings.

The release trigger is a single run-on condition turning on offtake agreements 'in form and substance and for a term ... reasonably acceptable' to two-thirds Lenders, with a good-faith negotiation proviso; whether the guarantee ever terminates depends on that undefined 'reasonably acceptable' standard. The date on which EGL's exposure ends is therefore genuinely contestable.

'Guarantor Obligations' is defined by reference to Section 2.01(a), which lumps together a payment guarantee owed to the Lenders and a funding obligation owed to the Borrower; provisions such as Section 2.07 and Section 2.03 then treat all Guarantor Obligations as payable to the Lenders. The composite definition does not sit easily with those sections.

'Material adverse effect on ... the business, financial condition, operations or performance or properties of the Guarantor since the date of this Agreement' supplies no threshold and the trailing 'since the date of this Agreement' dangles awkwardly from the list. Materiality and the baseline for measuring it are both left at large.

This defines 'Obligations' for the Borrower as the 'Borrower Obligations', while the 'Borrower Obligations' definition is itself built on 'the Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement)' — a circle a court would have to break. Section 4.02(c)'s survival of 'the Obligations' depends on which meaning applies.

The priority is limited to 'the purposes of and to the extent of the matters covered by this Agreement', a self-referential qualifier that leaves it uncertain which matters are 'covered' when the Credit Agreement addresses the same subject. The scope of the override is the whole question.

Section 2.01(b) opens 'Anything herein or in any other Loan Document to the contrary notwithstanding' and caps liability by reference to fraudulent-conveyance law, which is a competing priority rule to this Section. The two override provisions are not sequenced against each other.

The $250,000,000 cap is expressed as applying only to 'the Borrower Obligation under this clause (iii)', leaving the pre-conditions guarantee in clause (i) and the Deficiency funding obligation in clause (ii) apparently uncapped; the singular 'Borrower Obligation' compounds the doubt. Whether EGL's aggregate exposure is capped is precisely the kind of dispute this wording invites.

Clause (ii) requires EGL to pay a Deficiency 'to the Borrower', yet Section 2.07 says payments hereunder are paid to the Lenders and Section 4.15 denies any non-party a right under this Agreement; the beneficiary of the funding obligation cannot be settled from Section 2.01(a) alone. Section 2.02(b) further says the Lenders need never give the notice that clause (ii) makes the trigger.

Clause (i) reads 'the obligations of the Guarantor hereunder are primary and notwithstanding the obligations of any other Person', a sentence with no predicate after 'notwithstanding'; what the primary character is meant to survive is left to reconstruction. The mechanical break changes what the clause asserts.

This makes the guarantee end on the earlier of the EGL Guarantee Release Date or full payment, but Section 2.01(a) sets three different periods (conditions satisfaction, Commercial Operations Date, Release Date) and Section 2.06 revives the guarantee after payment is returned. The termination architecture cannot be read consistently across those provisions.

The first sentence — 'The Borrower shall notify the Guarantor ... that the Guarantor provides to the Borrower the amount of the Deficiency' — is missing a verb of demand and does not state on its face whether notice is a condition precedent to EGL's funding obligation. The certification requirement is also attached only to the Facility Agent's notice, not the Borrower's.

Section 2.01(a)(ii) makes receipt of notice under this subsection the trigger of the funding obligation, while Section 2.02(b) says the Agent and Lenders have no obligation ever to give such a notice. Read together the obligation may be rendered wholly discretionary.

This disclaims any obligation to issue a Deficiency notice, yet Section 2.01(a)(ii) conditions EGL's funding obligation on 'the Guarantor receives notice of such Deficiency as set forth in Section 2.02(a)'. Whether the funding covenant can be enforced without a notice is left unresolved.

The subsection is lettered (d) with no (c) or (e) in the Agreement, and it says funds 'shall be provided by way of a contribution to the capital ... or ... an Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loan' without saying who elects between them. The election is then assumed in the second sentence ('If the Guarantor decides').

'to pay the cost or cost that has created the Deficiency' is a repeated garble (plainly intended as 'cost or costs'), appearing twice. The error is small but it is the operative description of the permitted use of funds.

The waiver refers to 'any event affecting any term of a Guaranteed Obligation', a capitalised term defined nowhere in this Agreement or its definitions section. The scope of the waived notice depends on what that undefined term captures.

Reinstatement is triggered only by the 'insolvency, bankruptcy, dissolution, liquidation or reorganization of the Guarantor', where a payment guarantee would ordinarily be reinstated on avoidance of a Borrower payment; the catch-all 'or otherwise' is then left to carry that work. Whether a clawback from the Borrower's estate revives the guarantee turns on that reading.

This says payments by the Guarantor 'will be paid to the Lenders', but Section 2.01(a)(ii) and Section 2.02(d) require Deficiency funds to be paid to the Borrower as capital or a subordinated loan. The two directions of payment are not reconciled.

'would ... reasonably be expect to result in a Material Adverse Effect' is ungrammatical, and the representation is qualified only 'to the knowledge of Guarantor' for threatened proceedings. The error is minor and does not obviously change the sense.

'shall at all time rank at least pari passu in right of payment in insolvency with all its other present and future senior Indebtedness' is drafted as a forward-looking covenant inside a representation, with a grammatical slip and no carve-out for secured debt. What 'senior Indebtedness' catches is not fixed here.

'none of the or governors or managers of the Guarantor' contains a plain drafting break — a noun is missing after 'the' — leaving the class of persons covered uncertain. The reference to 'Disclosed Matters' also imports a term defined only elsewhere.

'expeditious and effective steps for the removal of such person' sets no time limit or measure of effectiveness, and the sentence converts a representation into a continuing covenant mid-paragraph. What performance discharges the obligation is not stated.
